spec_issues: The data rules are unusually detailed and consistent across prompt, CONTRACT.md and reviewer policy. The shipped 526 attempts may be used for anything, and so may everything derived from them (tasks/lean-validity/tests/task/review.py:7-10, 45-53). Every other miniF2F copy, including third-party proof attempts on miniF2F statements, is forbidden (review.py:56-62). Every trial that touched miniF2F used it only for decontamination, which the rule allows (review.py:63-65).

'The answer has to come from the model, not hand-written rules' is enforced as 'hand-written rules or regexes must not be the source of the prediction' (review.py:19-23). The rubric does not cover hand-written rule detectors fed as features into a learned head. Gemini cnnjfd shipped exactly that. One of its features is a blacklist of specific Mathlib identifiers mined from errors (`sq_pos`, `Int.cast_succ`, `Nat.factorial_mul` ...), alongside detectors it describes as having 'zero false positives on validation.jsonl' (trajectory [205]). The reviewer accepted it ('The 27 regex structural features are only inputs to the trainable heads'). Under a strict reading this is a partial hand-written validity checker. It did not affect any winner (23.4 at $10).

No trial accessed the inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks dataset, the benchmark repo or frontierml.org. The only 'frontier-ml' hits in Gemini 15ey73 and DeepSeek o0vki2 are the local /opt/frontier-ml harness directory.
verifier_issues: Reward = 2 x macro_F1 - 1, clamped to [0, 1] (task.yaml score_normalization: floor 0.5, ceiling 1.0). A classifier below chance therefore scores 0: Muse 57iczy had macro F1 0.397, below the 0.5 coin-flip floor. The held-out set is 3,540 attempts on 295 theorems.

The held-out statements are one-edit variants (a changed numeric literal and/or renamed variables) of statements drawn from the same public pools that agents may train on: Lean Workbook, Goedel-Pset and FormalMATH (tasks/lean-validity/tests/task/pipeline/statements.py:1-13). Verbatim copies were pruned in a late fix ('Before 2026-09-26 unmutated candidates were kept, which put 26% of the shipped held-out statements verbatim in public pools', statements.py:10-12). Training on these pools is therefore close to in-distribution by design. This rewards large self-labeled corpora, which is what the top runs built.

Local estimates overstate held-out F1 a great deal when agents validate on random splits of validation-derived mutants. Muse 57iczy reported 'Random-split eval macro F1 reached 0.9075' (final message [93]) and scored 0.397. Gemini cnnjfd's threshold curve showed 0.81 (trajectory [349]) and it scored 0.617. Theorem-grouped CV, as used by the Opus and Astra runs, tracked the held-out score far better.
task_level.noise: Opus orders cleanly (37.6, 45.3, 57.5), and so do Fable (28.6, 40.7, 43.2) and Gemini (23.4, 28.3, 32.5). Astra (37.5, 29.8, 35.8), DeepSeek (7.5, 29.1, 22.1) and Muse (0, 7.0, 0.1) do not. No standard error is published. With 3,540 attempts clustered in 295 theorems, a 1-2 point (0.005-0.01 macro F1) swing between near-identical models is plausible. The $10 winner is a dead heat: Opus 1qvy9h 37.55 vs Astra 2e28vk 37.51, 0.04 points apart. Opus wins $50 (45.3 vs Fable 40.7) and $200 (57.5 vs 43.2) clearly.
task_level.elicitation: The best runs spent heavily on CPU labeling farms and H100 fine-tuning (Opus $200: $168.5 wallet; Astra $200: $169). Most of the gain came from building tens to hundreds of thousands of attempts on public statement pools, labeled with Lean. Runs that used only the 526 shipped attempts plus mutants (DeepSeek 5xiz84, Muse 57iczy) or a zero-shot prompt (DeepSeek o0vki2) scored much lower. All Gemini runs are re-runs (-r2).
task_level.epoch_rationale: All 18 passed review. I found no false positive, false negative or infrastructure zero. The one grey-area trial (Gemini cnnjfd, regex features into a learned head) wins nothing. The $10 Opus/Astra tie (0.04 points) is noise, not a scoring defect.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: This is mostly real ML engineering: generate proof attempts with open provers on public statement pools, mutate them, label everything with Lean, fine-tune a prover LM (usually Goedel-Prover-V2-8B) as a sequence classifier, and calibrate the threshold on the shipped file. The benchmark-specific edge is that the held-out statements are near-variants of public pool statements and the shipped file is drawn from the same pipeline, both of which the rules allow. The only rule-adjacent behaviour is Gemini cnnjfd's hand-written error detectors.
